Extending the scope of these energy efficiency improvements to essential community facilities, such as the Clinic and Daycare—initially identified in the original audits—could further amplify community-wide benefits. Implementing similar retrofit strategies across these additional buildings could yield further reductions in energy use and operational costs, without necessitating significant alterations to the building's construction. Weather events and shifting flight schedules can cause delays at any time of year. All supplies must be externally sourced, either shipped ahead of time by barge, trucked from Bethel via seasonal ice road, or delivered by plane, and all hazardous waste must be removed at additional cost. Price increases and supply chain demands caused by the global effects of the COVID-19 pandemic were significant barriers to this project and exacerbated existing logistics difficulties for a construction project in rural Alaska. Challenges and Considerations The project faced significant hurdles, primarily from Akiachak’s remote location and compounded supply chain disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.
